rules.title: Start URL is not reachable (4xx/5xx or network error)
rules.description: The URL the audit started from does not return a successful response. 4xx pages are not indexed and 5xx/network errors slow crawling and eventually drop URLs from the index. Almost every other result in this report is incomplete as a consequence.
rules.fix: Check that the URL is correct and publicly reachable (DNS, TLS, firewall/WAF rules for crawlers, deployment status). If the content moved, redirect permanently (301/308).
rules.verify: Fetch the URL and confirm a 200 response.

sources.title: Google: HTTP status codes, network and DNS errors

rules.title: robots.txt returns a server error or is unreachable
rules.description: robots.txt responded with 5xx/429 or could not be fetched. RFC 9309 requires crawlers to assume complete disallow; Google pauses crawling and later falls back to the last cached copy (up to 30 days).
rules.fix: Make /robots.txt return 200 (with rules) or 404 (no rules). Never 5xx.
rules.verify: Fetch /robots.txt and confirm status 200 or 404.

rules.title: robots.txt exceeds 500 KiB
rules.description: Google processes only the first 500 KiB of robots.txt; rules after that limit are ignored. Yandex documents a similar 500 KB limit.
rules.fix: Consolidate rules (wildcards, directory prefixes) to bring the file under 500 KiB.
rules.verify: Check file size of /robots.txt.

rules.title: robots.txt blocks the whole site for search crawlers
rules.description: The homepage is disallowed for a major search crawler (Googlebot, Bingbot or YandexBot). Blocked URLs cannot be crawled; they may still be indexed without content if linked.
rules.fix: Remove the blanket "Disallow: /" for search crawlers. Use noindex (on crawlable pages) to keep specific pages out of the index.
rules.verify: Re-test robots.txt for Googlebot/Bingbot/YandexBot against the homepage.

sources.title: Google: Block Search indexing with noindex

rules.exceptions: Intentional for staging/private sites. Do not apply to sites that must stay out of search.

rules.title: crawl-delay is not honoured by Google or Yandex
rules.description: robots.txt sets Crawl-delay. Google does not support it; Yandex has ignored it since 2018 (use the Crawl rate setting in Yandex Webmaster). Bing does honour it.
rules.fix: Keep crawl-delay only if you target Bing (or other crawlers that honour it); manage Google/Yandex crawl rate in their webmaster tools.
rules.verify: No verification needed; informational.

rules.title: No sitemap is discoverable
rules.description: robots.txt has no Sitemap: directive and /sitemap.xml is not available. Sitemaps help search engines discover URLs, especially on large or new sites.
rules.fix: Publish an XML sitemap of canonical, indexable URLs and reference it with "Sitemap: https://…" in robots.txt.
rules.verify: Fetch the sitemap URL from robots.txt and confirm a valid <urlset>.

sources.title: Google: Build and submit a sitemap

rules.exceptions: Small sites with complete internal linking can be discovered without a sitemap.

rules.title: Sitemap lists URLs blocked by robots.txt
rules.description: URLs listed in the sitemap are disallowed in robots.txt. Sitemaps should list URLs you want crawled and indexed; the conflict wastes crawl signals.
rules.fix: Remove blocked URLs from the sitemap, or unblock them if they should be indexed.
rules.verify: Re-run the crawl and confirm no sitemap URL is robots-blocked.

sources.title: Google: Build and submit a sitemap

rules.title: Pages return 5xx server errors
rules.description: 5xx (and 429) responses make Google slow down crawling; persistent errors lead to URLs being dropped from the index.
rules.fix: Fix the server-side error; for maintenance return 503 with Retry-After briefly.
rules.verify: Re-fetch affected URLs and confirm 2xx.

sources.title: Google: HTTP status codes, network and DNS errors

rules.title: Pages could not be fetched (timeout, DNS, TLS or connection error)
rules.description: The crawler could not get any HTTP response. Search engines treat network and DNS errors like server errors.
rules.fix: Check DNS, TLS certificates, firewall/WAF rules for crawler user agents, and server timeouts.
rules.verify: Re-fetch affected URLs.

sources.title: Google: HTTP status codes, network and DNS errors

rules.title: Internal links point to 4xx pages
rules.description: Internal links lead to pages returning 4xx. Users hit dead ends and crawlers waste requests; 4xx pages are not indexed.
rules.fix: Update links to the correct live URL or add a 301 redirect for moved content.
rules.verify: Re-crawl and confirm no internal link targets return 4xx.

sources.title: Google: HTTP status codes, network and DNS errors

rules.title: External links point to unreachable or 4xx/5xx pages
rules.description: Outbound links return errors. This degrades user experience and source quality.
rules.fix: Update or remove the broken outbound links.
rules.verify: Re-check outbound link status.
rules.appliesWhen: Only when external link checking is enabled (--check-external).

rules.title: Links that crawlers cannot follow
rules.description: Anchor elements without an href (or with javascript:/# hrefs) are not followed by Google. Navigation must use <a href="…"> with resolvable URLs.
rules.fix: Render navigation as …; keep JS click handlers as progressive enhancement.
rules.verify: Inspect raw HTML for <a> elements with real href values.

rules.title: Internal links without anchor text
rules.description: Links have no text (no inner text, aria-label or image alt). Google uses anchor text to understand the linked page.
rules.fix: Add descriptive anchor text, or an alt attribute on linked images.
rules.verify: Inspect link markup.

rules.title: Redirect chains (more than one hop)
rules.description: URLs redirect through multiple hops. Google follows up to 10 hops but recommends redirecting directly to the final URL; chains slow crawling and users.
rules.fix: Point the first URL (and internal links) directly at the final destination.
rules.verify: Re-fetch and confirm a single hop.

sources.title: Google: HTTP status codes, network and DNS errors

rules.title: Redirect loop or too many redirects
rules.description: The redirect sequence loops or exceeds the hop limit; the page cannot be reached.
rules.fix: Fix the redirect rules so the chain terminates in a 200 page.
rules.verify: Re-fetch and confirm a final 200.

sources.title: Google: HTTP status codes, network and DNS errors

rules.title: Internal links go through temporary redirects
rules.description: Internally linked URLs respond with 302/303/307. Temporary redirects are a weaker canonicalisation signal than permanent ones (301/308).
rules.fix: Use 301/308 for permanent moves and update internal links to the final URL.
rules.verify: Re-fetch and check redirect status codes.

rules.title: Meta refresh redirect
rules.description: The page uses <meta http-equiv="refresh">. Google treats instant meta refresh as permanent and delayed refresh as temporary; server-side redirects are preferred.
rules.fix: Replace with a server-side 301/308 redirect.
rules.verify: Re-fetch and confirm an HTTP redirect.

rules.title: Pages are far from the start page (click depth > 4)
rules.description: Pages are only reachable after many link hops from the start URL. Deep pages tend to be discovered and recrawled less often. Depth is measured from the crawl start and may differ from real navigation.
rules.fix: Improve internal linking (hubs, categories, related links, breadcrumbs) so important pages are within a few clicks.
rules.verify: Re-crawl and compare click depth.

sources.title: Google: Large site owner's guide to managing crawl budget

rules.title: Sitemap URLs with no internal links
rules.description: URLs listed in the sitemap received no internal links from crawled pages. Orphan pages rely on the sitemap alone for discovery and get no internal link signals. Result is limited to the crawled portion of the site.
rules.fix: Link to these pages from relevant hub/category pages, or remove them from the sitemap if obsolete.
rules.verify: Re-crawl and confirm inlinks > 0.

sources.title: Google: Build and submit a sitemap

rules.title: Filter/sort parameters create many crawlable URL variants
rules.description: Internal links expose many URLs that differ only by query parameters (filters, sorting, facets) for the same path. Google warns that faceted navigation can generate a large number of URLs that consume crawl capacity and slow the discovery of new content.
rules.fix: If filtered URLs don't need to be in search, prevent crawling (robots.txt disallow for the parameters, URL fragments instead of query parameters, or rel=nofollow on filter links); if some do, keep a consistent parameter order and return 404 for empty combinations. rel=canonical helps consolidate but does not stop crawling.
rules.verify: Re-crawl and count parameter variants per path; check Crawl Stats in Search Console.
rules.exceptions: Small sites rarely have a crawl-capacity problem; pagination parameters alone are expected.

sources.title: Google: Managing crawling of faceted navigation URLs
